regions.region: upper half: title, abstract, and two-column introduction
regions.finding: The abstract states the paper-level aza-Prins scope and regioselectivity claim. The introduction discusses utility and cited prior methods; these broad claims and literature examples were not duplicated as experiments of this paper.

Generic alpha-sulfonamido-allene 1 and aldehyde 2 are proposed to form Int-1/Int-2 under acid and then possible products A-C after X-minus capture. This is classified as a mechanism, not a performed experiment.

The prose identifies Table 1 entry 1 and summarizes the optimization series. It reports 16 h for entry 1, conflicting with the 21 h shown in Table 1 on page 2; the record retains the table-row time and flags the conflict.

regions.region: lower-left author footnote and ESI notice
regions.finding: The article states that ESI exists, but no supplementary file was explicitly supplied or associated in this workspace; no SI-only procedure or characterization detail was imported.

unresolved: Table 1 entry 1 duration conflicts between page-1 prose (16 h) and page-2 table (21 h).
Generic R groups and X-minus in Scheme 1 preclude fully specified structures.
ESI availability is stated, but the SI itself was not provided or associated.

regions.finding: All 13 Fe(III)/TMSCl optimization rows were extracted independently, including catalyst and solvent substitutions, MgSO4 footnote addition, NMR yields, isolated yield for entry 4, recovered 1a, and source dashes without coercing them to zero.

All nine aldehyde-scope rows were extracted independently with shared FeCl3/TMSCl/CH2Cl2/30 degree C conditions, row-specific time and isolated yield, 1.5/2.0 equivalent overrides, and the entry-8 89% conversion kept separate from product yield.
The 1.1158 g paraformaldehyde experiment giving 3j in 70% yield was extracted as a separate reported experiment rather than merged with Table 2 entry 9 (74%).

regions.region: upper-right Table 3, reaction arrow, and footnotes
regions.finding: All eight 1b aldehyde-scope rows were extracted independently. The arrow supplies the 10 h default; footnotes override entry 6 to 14 h and entry 8 to 36 h. The source's conflicting reuse of label 2c for 4-chlorobenzaldehyde here versus 2-chlorobenzaldehyde in Table 2 is retained as unresolved.

regions.region: lower-right Scheme 2 and adjacent Suzuki-coupling prose
regions.finding: Three distinct Suzuki experiments were extracted: 3j with phenylboronic acid to 6a (85%), 3j with 2-furylboronic acid to 6b (90%), and 3b with phenylboronic acid to 6c (85%), each with the full arrow conditions.

unresolved: Most table rows omit exact batch scale, atmosphere, workup, and purification; the unavailable SI was not inferred.
Complex cyclic product structures remain machine-unverified and therefore have null SMILES.
The yield basis for Equation (1) and Scheme 2 is not stated.
Source label 2c denotes different positional isomers in Tables 2 and 3.

regions.finding: The FeCl3/TMSCl-promoted intermediate 7 and its R1 = H versus R1 = Ph branches through proposed intermediates 8/9 to products 3/4 were extracted as one mechanism record, not as performed experiments.

regions.region: left-column conclusion, acknowledgments, and lower reference list
regions.finding: The conclusion repeats the paper-level scope claim, while the remainder is acknowledgments and references. Cited prior literature and reproduced-results acknowledgments were not converted into new reaction records.
Crystal data for 3j and 4a are characterization statements, not independent synthetic experiments; references are prior work and were not attributed to this paper as new experiments.

unresolved: Scheme 3 is generic and proposed; R groups and intermediate structures are not fully specified as machine-verifiable molecules.
No additional experimental procedures are present on this page.
